title: The Canton System (Guangzhou as the only port for foreign trade)
summary: In 1757 the Qing court designated Guangzhou (Canton) as the only port for foreign commerce. Trade there was run by a monopoly of licensed Chinese merchants, the co-hong, under government officials, and foreign merchants could stay only during a trading season from April to September. China was forced to abandon the system after the First Opium War, which ended in 1842.

uncertainty.note: Start is the 1757 decision. Other sources date the formal co-hong monopoly to 1760; those pages were not used for the dates. The end year follows the EBSCO title (1757–1842).

importance.justification: Shaped Qing foreign trade for about eight decades and fed the tensions that led to the First Opium War.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the end date: EBSCO ties the end to the First Opium War and the 1842 settlement, while the Academy page covers only the early period; the 1842 end is from the EBSCO title and text. The Opium War link is listed as related; EBSCO says tensions including the opium trade led to the war, but I did not treat the system as its sole cause.
